abkhazia.title: Flag of Abkhazia

colors.note: Four of the seven alternating stripes; represent Islam.
Three of the seven stripes and the open hand; represent tolerance and the Christian population.
Canton; represents statehood and political courage.

desc:
- Seven alternating green and white horizontal stripes (starting with green) with a red canton bearing a white open right hand and seven white five-pointed stars arranged in an arc
- The seven stripes and seven stars represent the seven historic districts of Abkhazia
- The open hand symbolises the Abkhaz concept of hospitality ('Apsua')
- The green stripes represent Islam; the white stripes represent Christianity, reflecting the nation's religious diversity
- Adopted on 23 July 1992 during the Georgian–Abkhaz conflict
- Abkhazia is a partially recognised state; its independence is recognised by Russia and a handful of other nations
- **Construction:** seven equal horizontal stripes alternating green and white (green at top and bottom)
- The canton occupies the upper-left four stripes in height
- The open hand is centred in the canton, palm outward
- Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- Abkhazia is a partially recognized territory with contested sovereignty
- Recognized by Russia but not by most of the international community
- Located on the Black Sea coast between Russia and Georgia
